prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Conservatives invite Britain to join a new kind of government built on responsibility, enterprise and social action. Against Labour’s record of debt, waste and top‑down control, we say real change comes from the Big Society, not big government: power devolved from the centre to people, professionals and local communities. We are all in this together.

Economy and public finances: We will restore stability, protect Britain’s credit rating and keep interest rates low by eliminating the bulk of the structural deficit over a Parliament, creating an independent Office for Budget Responsibility and starting with an emergency Budget. We will cut at least £6bn of waste now, freeze most public sector pay for a year (protecting the lowest paid), streamline Whitehall and quangos, and stop Labour’s “jobs tax” (National Insurance rise) for most workers and employers. We’ll build a balanced, investment‑ and export‑led, hi‑tech, green economy: lower and simpler business taxes, lighter regulation, stronger R&D and STEM, better access to credit, and a safer banking system under Bank of England prudential supervision with a bank levy. We’ll boost skills, apprenticeships and FE freedom; create a single Work Programme with payment by results, tougher conditionality and support to start a business; and control immigration with an annual non‑EU limit and a stricter student visa system.

Spreading prosperity and infrastructure: We’ll grow the private sector in every region, deliver high‑speed rail (not a third Heathrow runway), reform rail franchising, roll out superfast broadband without Labour’s phone tax, and empower business‑led local enterprise partnerships, letting communities keep more of the proceeds of growth.

Public services and transparency: Good government costs less. We will publish spending and performance data, expand diverse provision, and back mutuals and co‑ops so staff can run services, with payment by results driving value.

Families, welfare and early years: We’ll make Britain the most family‑friendly country—recognising marriage and civil partnerships in the tax system, ending the couple penalty in tax credits, freezing council tax for two years with council partnership, extending flexible working and shared parental leave, protecting childhood from commercialisation, refocusing Sure Start on early intervention, and funding 4,200 more health visitors.

NHS: We’ll increase funding in real terms each year, scrap target‑driven bureaucracy, give patients choice of any qualified provider, empower GPs to commission, publish results openly, expand 24/7 urgent care, create a Cancer Drugs Fund, and integrate health and social care budgets, while backing carers and palliative care. Social care will be based on voluntary insurance, not a compulsory “death tax.”

Schools: We’ll raise standards with rigorous teaching and discipline, phonics and tougher exams, more great teachers (Teach First/Now, Troops to Teachers), technical academies, and a pupil premium. Parents and trusted providers will open new, high‑quality schools; strong schools will gain academy freedoms; failing schools will be transformed.

Crime and borders: We will fight crime and anti‑social behaviour, get police out from behind desks, introduce elected police commissioners, be tough on knives and binge‑drinking disorder, reform prisons for rehabilitation with payment by results, and create a Border Police Force.

Politics, localism and liberty: We will clean up Westminster (recall for corrupt MPs, donation caps, lobbying rules), cut the cost of politics and quangos, and give people real power—local referendums, neighbourhood planning, community rights to run services, and elected mayors. We will roll back the database state: scrap ID cards, reform DNA retention, replace the Human Rights Act with a UK Bill of Rights, and restore common‑sense safeguards.

Energy and environment: We will lead a low‑carbon, secure energy future—smart grid and meters, nuclear (without subsidy), CCS, offshore wind, a Green Investment Bank, a floor price for carbon, and a Green Deal to cut bills. We’ll protect habitats, reform fisheries and farming for sustainability, uphold high animal welfare, expand tree planting, and move towards a zero‑waste society.

Foreign policy, defence and aid: We will create a National Security Council, back our forces (repair the Military Covenant, reform procurement, retain Trident, succeed in Afghanistan), and pursue a liberal Conservative foreign policy—active, principled and hard‑headed. In Europe we’ll be positive but prevent any further power transfer without a referendum, seek repatriation in key areas, and never join the Euro. We will honour 0.7% aid by 2013, make it fully transparent and results‑driven, focus on the poorest, and lead on malaria, trade and climate‑smart development.
